Virtual Microscope: Observing Mitosis

Use the mouse like a microscope user: choose a prepared slide, pan the specimen, adjust coarse/fine focus, change objectives, and identify cells in different stages of mitosis.
Microscope view
Onion root tip • plant cells
40× total Focus: near sharp
Drag inside the circular field to move the slide. Start at 4× objective, center an area of interest, focus, and then move to higher magnification. At 40× objective (400× total magnification), click one of the target cells and identify its stage.

Use practice mode to observe real micrographs. For easiest use, leave markers visible. If you want more challenge, hide them.
What to look for
Interphase: diffuse chromatin; intact nucleus
Prophase: chromosomes condense and darken
Metaphase: chromosomes line up near the center
Anaphase: sister chromatids separate toward opposite poles
Telophase: two chromosome groups; two forming nuclei
Plant vs. animal: onion cells are box-like; whitefish cells are rounder
